groups.title: Form Actions Concepts
groups.question: Your todo page has forms to create and delete items, and invalid input should show an error next to the field. Explain how SvelteKit form actions work.

followUps.Defining actions in plus page.server.ts: How do form actions receive a form's POST?
followUps.Named actions for multiple forms on one: How do named actions let one page have several forms?
followUps.Returning validation errors from actions: How does fail() return errors to the form?

evidence.text: +page.server.ts exports an actions object.
Forms on the page post to these actions.
Mutation logic lives next to the page that uses it.
Each action has a name, like create or delete.
A form targets one with action set to ?/name.
Each form's logic stays in its own handler.
fail returns a status like 400 with error data.
The page stays where it is.
The page reads the result through its form prop and shows the errors.

groups.title: Schema Validation
groups.question: Your action reads form fields by hand and crashes when a field is missing. Explain how you would validate form data safely.

followUps.Zod schema validation for form data: Why validate form data with Zod in the action?
followUps.Parsing FormData with Object.fromEntries: Why convert FormData before parsing it?

evidence.text: Form data can contain anything, regardless of the HTML form.
A Zod schema checks types and required fields.
It returns readable errors for each field.
FormData is not a plain object.
Object.fromEntries turns it into a plain object Zod can parse.
All values arrive as strings, so numbers and booleans need conversion.

groups.title: Progressive Enhancement
groups.question: Your forms reload the whole page on submit, and you want likes to appear instantly. Explain progressive enhancement with use:enhance.

followUps.Enhance directive for JavaScript-enhance: What does use:enhance change, and what happens without JavaScript?
followUps.Custom enhance callback for optimistic u: How would you use a custom enhance callback for an optimistic update?

evidence.text: use:enhance submits the form with fetch instead of a full reload.
Without JavaScript, the form still works as a normal submission.
This is progressive enhancement: it works first and improves with JavaScript.
A callback passed to use:enhance runs before submission and receives the result.
The UI can be updated before the server responds.
It can roll back on failure or handle redirects itself.

notEnough: Only saying you pass a function.

groups.title: Invalidation After Mutations
groups.question: After saving, the page sometimes shows old data, and refreshing after a submit sends the form again. Explain how SvelteKit handles data after mutations.

followUps.Automatic data invalidation after action: What happens to load data after a successful enhanced action?
followUps.Redirect after POST to prevent duplicate: Why redirect with 303 after a successful POST?

evidence.text: By default use:enhance re-runs load functions after success.
The page shows fresh data without a manual refresh.
A custom callback can change or skip this behaviour.
Throwing redirect with 303 sends the browser to a new page with a GET.
Refreshing then repeats the GET, not the POST.
This prevents accidental duplicate submissions.
